title: Personal Agent — CandidateAssertion
description: Schema for a single CandidateAssertion: a typed, evidence-bound extraction awaiting human review (CandidateAssertion node). This is the pre-confirmation artifact emitted by skill 05 (candidate_extraction) from EvidenceItems produced by skills 01–04, scoped by skill 06, then judged at the confirmation gate (skill 07) and, once confirmed, routed by skill 08 (pack_router) into one of the 14 user.* packs — where it becomes a base instance record (../schemas/record.base.schema.json). A candidate is therefore NOT a base record: it does not extend record.base.schema.json. It carries the lighter contract §8 / skill-05 field set and uses `concise_claim` + `validation_status` where a promoted record uses `statement` + `review_status`. The `candidate_type` ↔ `proposed_target_pack` pair is the 1:1 total router from ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6; this schema enforces that mapping so a candidate cannot propose a pack its type does not route to. Gate G1 (≥1 evidence_ref) and Gate G2 (non-empty scope) apply already at the candidate stage. Pack catalog: ../spec/03-pack-catalog.md; routing & lifecycle: ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §1/§6; base record (post-promotion shape): ../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §7. (구 코드명: 후보 타입 DomainSpecificCandidate→DomainOverlayCandidate, ProjectGoalCandidate→ProjectMemoryCandidate.)

candidate_id.description: Stable candidate identifier. Follows the instance id grammar <subject>.<recordkind>.NNN (e.g. logotekton.candidate.001 or logotekton.heuristic_cand.014). On confirmation+routing (skill 08) it maps to the base record `id`; on rejection it is retained for audit/drift. Pattern mirrors record.base.schema.json `id`.

candidate_type.description: One of the 14 candidate types (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6). Determines `proposed_target_pack` via the 1:1 total router (enforced by the allOf rules below). DomainOverlayCandidate was DomainSpecificCandidate; ProjectMemoryCandidate was ProjectGoalCandidate (구 코드명).

concise_claim.description: The candidate claim in one concise sentence, written in observed-behavior language, not guessed psychology (Gate G4). This is the candidate-stage analogue of the base record `statement`; on promotion the (possibly edited) text becomes `statement`. Keep it scoped and checkable — e.g. 'Prefers terse, bulleted replies in code-review contexts' rather than 'Likes things short'.

evidence_refs.description: ≥1 EvidenceItem id/ref the claim is `supported_by`/`extracted_from` (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §4). Gate G1: no evidence-free candidate — a candidate that cannot cite at least one EvidenceItem must not be created. Carried unchanged into the base record's `evidence_refs` on promotion.

confidence.description: 0..1 extraction confidence that this candidate faithfully reflects the subject (not certainty that it should be a rule — that is the human's call at the gate). May be derived from `confidence_inputs`. Carried into the base record `confidence`; note the base rule that confidence < 0.7 requires counterexamples applies after promotion.

scope.description: Where/when the claim is asserted to hold (e.g. 'code-review sessions on own repos', 'external email only'). Gate G2: no unscoped candidate — assigned/refined by skill 06 (scope_context). A candidate may enter with a provisional scope; it must be non-empty before it can pass the confirmation gate.

sensitivity.description: Privacy class, same enum as record.base.schema.json `sensitivity`. Set as early as extraction so the confirmation gate (skill 07) and privacy_boundary (skill 09) can require a BoundaryRule before any sensitive/restricted candidate is promoted (Gate G5).

proposed_target_pack.description: The single canonical user.* pack this candidate is proposed to route into on confirmation (skill 08 pack_router). MUST match the 1:1 mapping for `candidate_type` (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6); the allOf rules below reject any other pairing. 'Proposed' because routing only happens after the gate confirms — pending candidates never enter a pack (Gate G3).

validation_status.description: Confirmation-gate state (skill 07), same value set as the base record `review_status` to keep one lifecycle vocabulary. pending = awaiting review; confirmed = approved (may promote); rejected = declined (retained for audit/drift); narrowed = approved with a tightened scope; sensitive = approved in principle but blocked on a BoundaryRule (Gate G5); deferred = revisit later. Only confirmed/narrowed candidates may promote to a pack (Gate G3); an edit is logged via review_audit.decision=edit while the status stays confirmed/narrowed.

extraction_method.description: How this candidate was produced, naming the upstream builder skill (01–04) or a manual/other source. evidence_capture=skill 01; session_mining=skill 02; elicitation_questioning=skill 03 (structured interview); diff_mining=skill 04 (before/after corrections). Records extraction provenance for traceability and for weighting `confidence_inputs` (e.g. diff_mining tends to carry strong correction_strength).

reliability.description: Evidence CHANNEL of this candidate, intended to carry unchanged into the promoted record's `reliability` (record.base.schema.json) — though the candidate→record promotion step is not yet wired (tools/pab.py promotion is a STUB; live compiler wiring pending, #9). behavioral = extracted from observed behavior/artifacts/corrections (Gate G4) — the default. self_reported = the subject described themselves in words. A self_reported candidate is a low-trust InterpretationClaim about the self: it must not be auto-confirmed on promotion and stays draft-only (does not earn standalone runtime authority or count toward maturity depth). Absent = behavioral. Lets an interior/motivational signal be carried without being laundered into behavioral evidence. Spec: spec/01-kernel-schema.md §7.1.
reliability.$comment: Most candidates are behavioral by construction (skills 01–04 mine behavior/diffs). self_reported is set when skill 03 elicitation captures a self-description that the subject states but no behavior yet confirms.

confidence_inputs.description: Optional explicit signals behind `confidence` (contract §8 / skill 05). Making the basis of a score legible keeps confidence auditable rather than a black-box number; a tool may recompute `confidence` from these.

explicit_statement.description: True if the subject stated this directly (e.g. 'always do X'), vs. it being inferred from behavior. Direct statements warrant higher confidence.

repetition_count.description: How many distinct EvidenceItems independently support the claim. Repeated support across sessions raises confidence and helps satisfy the base rule that broad records need repeated support or explicit confirmation.

correction_strength.description: 0..1 strength of any corrective signal behind the claim — how firmly the subject changed/rejected an output (typically from diff_mining). Strong corrections are high-signal evidence of a real preference.

recency.description: 0..1 recency weight of the supporting evidence (1 = most recent). Newer evidence weighs more so the agent tracks current, not stale, behavior; feeds drift detection.

contradiction_count.description: Number of EvidenceItems that conflict with the claim. Higher counts lower confidence and may force narrowed/deferred at the gate or a counterexample on the promoted record.

domain_specificity.description: 0..1 how domain-bound the claim is (1 = highly domain-specific). Informs `scope` tightness and whether the claim belongs in user.domain_overlays vs. a general pack.

evidence_quality.description: 0..1 quality/directness of the cited evidence (e.g. a verbatim correction scores higher than a loose inference). Guards confidence from being inflated by weak sources.

$comment: A CandidateAssertion is the pre-confirmation artifact, so this schema deliberately does NOT $ref record.base.schema.json — it carries the contract §8 / skill-05 field set (candidate_id, candidate_type, concise_claim, evidence_refs, confidence, scope, sensitivity, proposed_target_pack, validation_status, extraction_method) and the optional confidence_inputs object. Vocabulary is shared with the base: `sensitivity` and `validation_status` reuse the base enums (validation_status mirrors review_status). Field correspondence on promotion (skill 08): candidate_id→id, concise_claim→statement, validation_status→review_status, evidence_refs/confidence/scope/sensitivity carried over, proposed_target_pack selects the destination user.* schema. The 14 allOf if/then rules pin candidate_type→proposed_target_pack to the 1:1 total router (../spec/01-kernel-schema.md §6) so the two fields cannot disagree. Gates already active at candidate stage: G1 (evidence_refs ≥ 1), G2 (non-empty scope), G4 (behavioral language in concise_claim), G5 (sensitive/restricted blocked on a BoundaryRule before promotion); G3 means pending candidates never reach a pack. Pack catalog: ../spec/03-pack-catalog.md.
